direction.title: Exception first: the problem owns the screen
direction.summary: The most urgent item is promoted out of the list into a full-width strip, with its position in the queue; every other row stays quiet. Use for time-pressured operations queues.

layout.skeleton: exception strip on top (item ID, location, deviation), the full queue table below, a due-next rail on the right
layout.focus: the deviation value at 40px tabular figures, with an 'n / total' position label
layout.desktop: 12-col; strip spans 12, table 8, rail 4 holding the next item due
layout.mobile: strip, then rail, then table as stacked rows

imagery.subject: none; location codes act as the visuals
imagery.fallback: location code set at 24px tabular figures

motion.effect: the value cross-fades; the strip edge pulses once

action.instruction: Focus jumps the table filter to the exception. Fill it from the brief's most urgent item
action.label: Focus [item ID] at [location]

interaction.focus: Use a two-tone focus ring (2 px paper with 2 px ink outside) on the primary control.
interaction.accent_role: Use the accent as a focal fill under accent_foreground. Check contrast before using it as text.
interaction.keyboard: Expose the primary control by keyboard and announce pending and completed states.

assumptions: Use only the project facts and assets in the brief.
handoff: Apply the composition to the actual content. Preserve the task and brand constraints. Fill label slots only with facts supplied by the brief. Use the source as design evidence. Verify the action, reading order and legibility at 390 px.
